body.x: AETECH (CEO Taehyung Park) announced that it will participate in CES 2026, to be held in Las Vegas, the United States, from January 6 to 9, as part of the INCHEON-IFEZ Pavilion.

AETECH is a resource circulation technology company that automates waste sorting using AI vision and robotics. To address structural challenges across the waste treatment industry, including high labor intensity, low sorting efficiency, and quality inconsistencies, the company develops solutions applicable to diverse sites by integrating AI vision and robotic control technologies grounded in real-world operational data.

Based on this technological foundation, AETECH has expanded its lineup to include the automatic sorting robot Atron, the urban resource circulation station Multi-tron, and the resource circulation automation facility Airo-MRF. In particular, Multi-tron features a compact AI robotics structure suitable for multifunctional urban spaces and received a CES 2026 Innovation Award in recognition of its innovation. These technologies target not only large-scale public sorting facilities but also improved accessibility to resource recovery within everyday urban living areas.

AETECH is advancing public and private sorting facility automation projects in Korea, building regional resource circulation infrastructure, and expanding overseas applications through global partnerships. The company continues to enhance its technology using waste data accumulated in real operational environments and to refine field-oriented solutions, proposing a new waste management structure that enables higher resource recovery rates and stable operations.

Having accumulated validation and commercialization results by applying AI-based waste-sorting automation technologies in real operating environments in Korea, AETECH currently operates more than 30 Atron robots across 11 public and private waste sorting facilities. The company stated that it has the largest number of installations in the domestic AI waste-sorting robot sector.

body.cap: Automatic sorting robot Atron | Image provided by AETECH

body.x: AETECH has also established a business foundation capable of meeting domestic public-sector demand for waste-sorting automation. Atron has been designated as an innovative product by the Public Procurement Service based on its commercial track record and technological reliability, allowing public institutions to procure the system through direct contracts without separate bidding procedures.

In overseas markets, collaboration discussions are underway in Asia and Oceania, including Japan and Singapore. In the Middle East, AETECH is reviewing the applicability of waste management automation in smart cities and urban infrastructure environments, with a focus on Dubai. In North America, the company is examining deployment opportunities in Canada, while in Europe, including Germany, it is validating technical applicability through proof-of-concept projects.

At CES 2026, AETECH plans to present its waste-sorting automation solutions that integrate AI vision and robotics. The exhibition aims to communicate the characteristics of its technologies and their diverse applications, focusing on AETECH’s resource circulation automation approach that spans from sorting automation to urban resource recovery.

Atron is an automatic sorting robot that combines AI vision-based recognition with robotic control technology to identify waste in real time and sort it according to predefined criteria. Its AI has been trained on 5.5 million real-world waste data points and can classify up to 96 items per minute with 99.3 percent accuracy. As Korea’s first commercial AI waste-sorting robot, Atron currently operates more than 30 units in public and private facilities, automating the sorting process. The company emphasized that it replaces repetitive, hazardous manual labor, thereby improving working conditions and operational efficiency.

body.cap: Urban resource circulation station Multi-tron | Image provided by AETECH

body.x: Multi-tron, also featured at the exhibition, is a compact, modular resource circulation station designed for installation and operation in urban and multipurpose spaces. It adopts a Dump & Go structure in which AI systems automatically recognize and sort waste upon disposal, enabling resource recovery functions in space-constrained environments such as public housing, shopping malls, and stadiums. By presenting an urban resource circulation model, Multi-tron complements the limitations of centralized, large-scale sorting infrastructure. Its innovation earned it a CES 2026 Innovation Award in the Smart Communities category.

Finally, Airo-MRF is a resource-circulation automation facility built on AETECH’s AI waste-sorting technology. Through sorting automation, it improves the operational ROI of resource recovery systems and enhances the quality of recovered recyclables, enabling the production of high-purity PET flakes. The facility uses a modular structure that allows flexible configuration based on site conditions and has received a Bronze Award at the 2025 Edison Awards in recognition of its technical completeness.

An AETECH official said that participation in CES 2026 aims to lay the groundwork for overseas expansion of its AI vision- and robotics-based resource circulation automation technologies. The company has gradually verified the applicability of its solutions in global environments, drawing on its accumulated commercialization experience and technological competitiveness at domestic waste sorting sites.

The official added that AETECH has participated in CES consistently over the past two years, using the exhibition not only to promote technology but also to assess global market demand and gather direct feedback. Through previous exhibitions, the company has confirmed interest from overseas buyers and public-sector stakeholders in AI-based waste-sorting technologies. It gained a deeper understanding of national differences in waste management environments and regulatory systems. These experiences have informed subsequent technology advancements and solution configurations.

body.cap: Resource circulation automation facility Airo-MRF | Image provided by AETECH

body.x: At CES 2026, AETECH plans to present a clearer business message and an integrated solution structure through the Incheon–IFEZ joint booth, building on prior exhibition experience. By introducing a technology approach that spans sorting automation, urban resource recovery, and distributed resource circulation infrastructure, the company aims to share a vision for resource circulation automation solutions demanded by global markets.

AETECH plans to pursue overseas expansion through a phased approach. In the near term, it will strengthen collaboration with local partners in countries where cooperation discussions are already underway, including Japan, Oceania, and Singapore, and focus on building structures that support distribution and operations. This strategy targets securing initial references and tailoring solution configurations and business models to national market characteristics.

In the mid- to long-term, AETECH plans to expand its applications in areas with high demand for automation, such as smart cities, public infrastructure, and urban resource circulation projects. The company aims to strengthen its position as an integrated resource circulation automation solution provider that delivers not only equipment but also operational efficiency improvements and enhanced resource recovery quality. AETECH also stated its intention to continue leveraging global exhibitions and networking to expand overseas partnerships and progressively refine region-specific market entry strategies.

Incheon Metropolitan City and the Incheon Free Economic Zone Authority announced that they will establish the INCHEON-IFEZ Pavilion in the LVCC North Hall at CES 2026, showcasing Incheon’s urban vision and innovative technologies as the city evolves from smart city development into the AI era. By linking various exhibition programs—including the 10 companies participating in the INCHEON-IFEZ Pavilion, Eureka Park, global pavilions, and the CES Innovation Award Showcase—the organizations will support the participation of 51 Incheon-based innovative companies at CES. Notably, 14 companies received CES Innovation Awards across 17 categories, marking a record-high achievement and demonstrating the technological competitiveness and global growth potential of Incheon’s innovation companies.
